Electrical panel constraint modeling was added to ResStock via OpenStudio-HPXML measures in 2025 to assess whether the existing panel has enough capacity or breaker space to accommodate new loads from an energy retrofit. For details on panel constraint modeling, refer to the ResStock Technical Reference Guide (Reyna, et al., 2025). This measure does not introduce new electrical loads or circuits, so it has no impact on the electrical panel. However, electrical panel metrics are included as a standard output for this and all other envelope measures. Any panel constraints appearing in the upgrade results reflect pre-existing conditions, as this measure does not worsen them. 4 Results This section first confirms the intended modeling approach for the upgrade by examining individual dwelling models, then presents the results if the upgrade were applied to the entire applicable building stock. 4.1 Single Building Example This section examines a dwelling unit in Colorado (climate zone 5B) that underwent the envelope package upgrade, which includes advanced air sealing, attic floor insulation, duct sealing and insulation, and drill-and-fill wall insulation. Table 3 presents the housing characteristics of the unit before and after the upgrade. To assess the package’s effectiveness, we compared the performance of the unit with the full upgrade to its performance when each of the four individual measures was applied separately. Table 3. Among these five scenarios, heating energy use shows the largest reduction, dropping from 105.5 MBtu in the baseline to 39.9 MBtu with the full upgrade, a 62% decrease.
